…es, non sine lessu tamen ob mortem Quesnelli capitis sui post Arnaldum æstimattissimi, a quo omnis hæc causa præsens ducta est. Non hic viri hujus vitæ historiam texere lubet, duo tantum iis, quæ jam de eo dicta sunt, memoratu digna juvat addere. Primum est scriptum quoddam ab ipso Quesnello Sacerdoti cuidam missum, qui abstersa tandem errorum caligine, sibi, & Ecclesiæ redditus illud prodidit. Regulæ erant 12. articulis comprehensæ, quibus sui in conversatione inter se & cum vario hominum genere uterentur. Summa ferme hæc erat: Unio, & concordia: arcani fides: circumspectio in sermone pro varia hominum conditione: amphibologia in variis capitibus Religionis: uti Christum in Eucharistia præsentem, neque tantum per fidem, aut figuram, ut heterodoxi, sed neque per transubstantiationem, aut substantialiter, sive realiter, ut Catholici ajunt, dici volebat: quomodo igitur? modo imperceptibili. In Sacramento pænitentiæ attritionis insufficientiam, & necessitatem contritionis perfectæ urgerent. Gratiam sufficientem, libertatem indifferentiæ, merita modo aperte impugnarent, modo per verborum ambages, ut pressis exitus pateat: Gratiam victricem unice extollant: & sic alia plura. Alterum est

Amstelodami extrema senectute ad mortis confinia deductus, quarto ante obitum die rogatis duobus testibus appellationem suam innovat, sicque accepto a Pastore suo viatico vixit 2. Decembris annorum 85. senecio.

…add two things to what has already been said about him that are worth noting. The first is a certain writing sent by Quesnel himself to a certain priest, who, having finally wiped away the mist of errors and being returned to himself and to the Church, produced it. They were rules comprised in 12 articles, which his followers were to use in conversation among themselves and with various kinds of men. The sum of it was almost this: Union and concord; fidelity to the secret; circumspection in speech according to the various conditions of men; ambiguity in various chapters of Religion; he wanted it to be said that Christ is present in the Eucharist, not only by faith or figure, as the heterodox say, but neither by transubstantiation, nor substantially or really, as the Catholics say: how then? in an imperceptible way. In the Sacrament of Penance, they would urge the insufficiency of attrition and the necessity of perfect contrition. They would openly attack sufficient grace, the liberty of indifference, and merits, sometimes directly and sometimes through the maze of words, so that an exit might be open for the pressured: let them exalt only victorious grace: and so many other things.

———— page break ————

The second is a notable testimony of truth given by the man himself. Quesnel, asked by his nephew Pinfon, a sculptor, to which party of those then litigating about matters of Religion he should adhere, responded by letter: "He should hold himself to the greater part of the faithful, or firmly adhere to the trunk of the tree of the Church; for he himself had not been provoked and compelled to foster these disputes so pertinaciously except by the injuries of the Jesuits." Pinfon asserted that he had heard the same from Quesnel's own mouth not only once, with the Bishop of Angers, Poncet de la Rivière, as witness in his *Reflexions consolatoires* . But from the time when madness swept the man away, in the year 1719, at the very end of his old age in Amsterdam and brought to the borders of death, four days before his passing, he renewed his appeal, having summoned two witnesses, and thus, having received viaticum from his Pastor, the old man lived on until December 2.

… Commissarii, quorum princeps Cardinalis Rohanus; Præses Concilii Noaillius dictus. Convenerunt ad 18. Octob. ex 18. Archiepiscopis septeni, ex 112. Episcopis triginta tres. Noaillius de sua quondam data libri præfatione, & mandato paullo ante vulgato præfatus, mox de Bullæ obscuritate, dubiisque inde nascituris concionabatur, mirantibus cæteris, quibus in ea clara omnia, & plana videbantur. Demonstrabat Rohanus, nullam esse ex 101 propositionem, cui non competat una ex censuris: Noaillius tamen, quantum poterat, contendebat, Bullam haud aliter, quam præfixa instructione, additisque quibusdam explicationibus, & restrictionibus acceptari posse. Rejecta hæc propositio fere ab omnibus, & ei a Cardinali Rohano quatuor articuli oppositi: 1. manifeste ex Bulla constare, ac tenendum esse, librum Quesnelli esse hæreticum: 2. illas 101 propositiones esse merito damnatas, & una ex subjectis censuris dignas: proinde 3. Bullam acceptari debere ante omnem ulteriorem explicationem; cum circa prædicta nec ambigua sit, nec obscura. 4. nulla alia prævia instructione opus esse, nisi qua fideles contra falsas Bullæ interpretationes præmunirentur. Finally, to cut us (whom you, expecting some small pension of money from our Papists, wretchedly lie in wait for), us, I say, to pieces with those most impudent insults for that reason? Do you, a nobody, call our most illustrious Princes, under whose leadership we waged those wars for the liberty of the Fatherland, in accordance with the royal Edicts themselves, approved by the assembly of the Gallican Orders, so slanderously, so impudently, so falsely, turbulent, and robbers and invaders of others' properties? Do you, who accuse us of contempt for the Magistrate, condemn him with most savage accusations? Here, certainly, you now show what your purpose was in publishing this entire sycophantic writing. You hide nothing from us. We know these frauds of yours; and we smell this new Papist charity of yours. But if we wanted to speak of your parent, a most impure man, or of yourself, a wicked, erroneous, and wandering man, what abundance of material would we now have, I ask, to speak and to write? of the Magistrate so harshly, learn, I say, not only to think well of our Magistrates and Princes, but also, regarding those things which you do not understand in their actions (for those things exceed the capacity of your talent), not to judge rashly at all. But yet, so that everyone may understand how undeservedly we, the Pastors of the Gallican Churches, are accused by this man, we respond, with God himself as witness: that we indeed rejoice that those idols, which had been erected for so long in contempt of God and were keeping so many thousands of men in vain superstition until now, have been removed from the eyes of men. For whether, says Paul, Christ is announced out of occasion or out of true spirit, we rejoice in this.
